key_insight: An uncertainty-aware framework translates predicted patient risks into ICU staffing plans, reporting a favorable balance between staffing costs and shortages.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support ICU staffing decisions under shift rigidity and hiring delays, but patient-outcome benefits remain unproven.
method: Model dynamic predictive uncertainty without changing the upstream risk model.
Use Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to assess extreme staffing-shortage exposure.
Feed risk-calibrated demand into hourly rolling-horizon scheduling with staffing delays.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on realistic MIMIC-IV trajectories compared cost–shortage trade-offs against deterministic and reactive baselines, with Pareto analysis and calibration-drift stress tests.
watch_item: The abstract reports retrospective trajectory-based evaluation, not prospective evidence of staffing feasibility or patient safety benefits.
paper_title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing
